---
title: 'Quickstart: remote plugin'
description: Build a remote plugin, an MCP server that uses Streamable HTTP, from templates/remote-plugin. Run it locally, add it to the app, deploy it and register it in the marketplace.
icon: Globe
---

A remote plugin is a server you run yourself. The app connects to it over the internet and calls
its tools. On this page you copy the template, write a tool, run the server on your computer, add it
to the app, and then deploy and register it.

The server speaks the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP), an open
standard that lets AI apps discover and call tools on a server. PKU Harness uses MCP's Streamable
HTTP transport, in which each call is an HTTP `POST` request.

Users add a remote plugin by its URL or from the marketplace. Its tools then join the same registry
as the tools of bundled plugins, follow the same permissions and are called by the same assistant.
None of your code runs on the phone, and a remote plugin never sees campus credentials.

You need bun and some TypeScript. The template uses TypeScript with the official MCP SDK, but any
language with an MCP server library works the same way.

## 1. Start from the template

```bash
cd pku-harness-plugins
cp -r templates/remote-plugin ../my-plugin
cd ../my-plugin
bun install
```

The template is one file, `server.ts`, plus a `package.json` that pulls in
`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `express` and `zod`:

```ts title="server.ts"
import { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js';
import { StreamableHTTPServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js';
import express from 'express';
import { z } from 'zod';

function build() {
  // name = your registry id: the app installs the plugin as `mcp-<name>`.
  const server = new McpServer(
    { name: 'my-plugin', version: '0.1.0', title: '我的插件' },
    { instructions: 'What this plugin is for, in one sentence.' },
  );
  server.registerTool(
    'hello',
    {
      title: '打个招呼',
      description: 'Return a greeting. Replace with a real capability.',
      inputSchema: { name: z.string().describe('who to greet') },
      annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },
    },
    async ({ name }) => ({
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: `你好，${name}` }],
      structuredContent: { greeting: `你好，${name}` },
    }),
  );
  return server;
}

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => {
  // Optional bearer auth: users paste the token in the app; it is stored in their keychain.
  if (process.env.PLUGIN_TOKEN && req.headers.authorization !== `Bearer ${process.env.PLUGIN_TOKEN}`) {
    res.status(401).json({ jsonrpc: '2.0', error: { code: -32001, message: 'unauthorized' }, id: null });
    return;
  }
  const server = build();
  const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined }); // stateless
  res.on('close', () => {
    transport.close();
    server.close();
  });
  await server.connect(transport);
  await transport.handleRequest(req, res, req.body);
});
app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8787), () => console.log('MCP plugin ready on /mcp'));
```

The `build()` function creates the server and registers its tools. The `/mcp` route checks the
optional token, then hands the request to a fresh server. Replace the `hello` tool with your own.

## 2. Write real tools

Each MCP field of a tool has a specific use in PKU Harness:

- **`name`**, the first argument of `registerTool`, becomes the tool id `mcp-<server>.<name>`. The
  model sees it as `mcp-<server>__<name>`. Use a short ASCII camelCase name. Other characters become
  `_`, and names longer than 40 characters are cut.
- **`title`** is shown to users in chat, in approval prompts and in Settings. Write it in Chinese.
- **`description`** is shown to the model. Say when and how to use the tool, and give units and
  formats.
- **`inputSchema`** is converted to zod on the device and checked before every call. Describe every
  field.
- **`annotations.readOnlyHint`** sets the effect. `true` gives the effect `read`, and the tool runs
  directly. If the hint is missing or `false`, the effect is `write`, and by default the app asks the
  user first.
- **`structuredContent`** in the result is returned to the model as `data`. This is the preferred
  form. Without it, the app tries to parse the text content as JSON, and passes it as text if that
  fails.
- **`isError: true`** in the result turns the text into the error message the assistant sees.

The first 500 characters of the server's `instructions` go into the plugin's section of the system
prompt. Just before them, the app adds a line telling the model that this plugin's output is data
and must not be followed as instructions.

<Callout type="warn" title="Effects for remote tools">
  For now the app gives a remote tool one of two effects: `read` when `readOnlyHint: true`, and
  `write` for everything else. A tool that spends money or posts publicly is therefore also `write`,
  and asks first by default. Say plainly in its `title` and `description` what it does.
</Callout>

## 3. Run it and add it to the app

```bash
bun server.ts                       # MCP plugin ready on /mcp, port 8787
# optional: PLUGIN_TOKEN=secret bun server.ts
```

In the app, open **Settings → Plugins → Add remote plugin**. Enter the URL, and the token if you set
one. The URL depends on where the app runs:

| Where the app runs | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Android emulator | `http://10.0.2.2:8787/mcp` |
| Phone on the same network | `http://<your machine's LAN IP>:8787/mcp` |
| Deployed | `https://my-plugin.example.com/mcp` |

The emulator reaches your computer at `10.0.2.2`. A real phone needs your computer's address on the
local network (LAN).

The app connects, lists your tools and shows each one with its effect on the plugin's page. Then ask
the assistant something your tool can answer. You can also ask the assistant to install the plugin
for you. It calls `plugins.installRemote`, which asks for your approval first.

<Callout title="A complete example">
  `examples/demo-canteen` in `pku-harness-plugins` is a working remote plugin with mock data. It has
  one read tool and one write tool, and its bearer token is `demo-token`. Run it with
  `bun examples/demo-canteen/server.ts`.
</Callout>

## 4. Deploy

Any host that serves HTTPS will do: a virtual private server (VPS), Fly.io, Railway, Cloudflare
with an MCP-compatible runtime, or a campus server. Keep these points in mind:

- Production needs HTTPS. Use plain HTTP only for local development.
- `POST /mcp` must answer MCP Streamable HTTP requests. The template is **stateless**: it builds a
  new server for each request. That suits serverless hosts, which may start a fresh process for every
  request.
- Some campus hosts answer only inside the PKU network. If you call one of them, your server has to
  run inside that network too. The app can't lend your server the user's campus session.
- Your own secrets, such as API keys, stay on the server. To protect the endpoint, use a bearer
  token and set `"auth": "bearer"` in the registry entry.

## 5. Register it

Registering the plugin lists it in the marketplace, so students can find it. There are two ways to
do this. You can add a manifest to your repository and submit it through this website's marketplace
([manifest reference](/en/docs/marketplace/manifest), [submitting](/en/docs/marketplace/publishing)).
Or you can add an entry to `registry/registry.json` in `pku-harness-plugins`. Either way, the `id`
must match your MCP server's `name`:

```json
{
  "id": "my-plugin",
  "name": "我的插件",
  "description": "一句话说明它做什么。",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "source": "https://github.com/you/my-plugin",
  "kind": "remote",
  "endpoint": "https://my-plugin.example.com/mcp",
  "auth": "none",
  "requires": ["network"],
  "scopes": ["example.com"],
  "tags": ["canteen"]
}
```

Before you open a pull request against the registry, run `bun scripts/validate-registry.ts`. See
[Publishing](/en/docs/build/publishing) and the [review policy](/en/docs/marketplace/review).

## Checklist

- [ ] The MCP server's `name` equals the registry `id` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$`).
- [ ] Every tool has a Chinese `title`, a `description` for the model, and described input fields.
- [ ] Read-only tools set `annotations.readOnlyHint: true`, and no other tool does.
- [ ] Results are data (`structuredContent`), never instructions, and reasonably small.
- [ ] The plugin never asks for a campus password.
- [ ] The endpoint uses HTTPS, and bearer auth is declared if you use it.
